title: Valproate and other mood stabilisers
blurb: Apply the MHRA valproate restrictions and the key safety checks for carbamazepine and lamotrigine.
question: Jordan, 24, is admitted with mania. A junior doctor suggests starting valproate because lithium needs blood tests. What should the nurse point out about starting valproate?

teach.body: Valproate, carbamazepine and lamotrigine are anticonvulsants also used in bipolar disorder. Each carries a specific hazard. Valproate harms the unborn child: it causes birth defects and neurodevelopmental disorders after exposure in pregnancy. Carbamazepine can cause serious skin, blood and liver reactions. Lamotrigine can cause a dangerous rash if the dose is increased too fast. In plain English: know the one big danger of each drug and the check that guards against it.

teach.caption: NICE CG185 1.10.29-1.10.35. Valproate is not started in primary care (1.2.8).

teach.body: Carbamazepine can cause blood, liver and skin disorders. People and carers are taught to seek immediate help for fever, rash, mouth ulcers, bruising or bleeding. The HLA-B*1502 allele, particularly in people of Han Chinese or Thai origin, is strongly linked to Stevens-Johnson syndrome, so test before starting in those groups. Hyponatraemia is a common side effect, and when stopping it for bipolar disorder the dose is reduced over at least 4 weeks.

Lamotrigine is used for bipolar depression, not mania: NICE says do not offer it to treat mania. Before starting: FBC, U&Es and LFTs. It interacts with valproate and needs slow dose titration. People must contact their doctor immediately if a rash develops while the dose is being increased, and tell the team if pregnant or planning pregnancy. Levels are not routine. Stop over at least 4 weeks.

Nurse Okoye explains that Jordan is under 55, so the MHRA rules mean valproate should not be started unless two specialists independently agree and document that no other effective, tolerated treatment exists or that the reproductive risks do not apply. For acute mania NICE suggests an antipsychotic such as haloperidol, olanzapine, quetiapine or risperidone first. She records the discussion and raises it at the ward round.

teach.text: The valproate under-55 rule covers men too, not just women. And a woman on valproate who wants to stop because of pregnancy plans should stop gradually under medical supervision, not abruptly on her own.

items: Valproate: not started under 55 unless 2 specialists independently agree and document.
Women and girls able to have children: Pregnancy Prevention Programme; men: contraception during and 3 months after.
Valproate checks: weight, FBC, LFTs at start, 6 months, then yearly; no routine levels.
Carbamazepine: HLA-B*1502 test in Han Chinese or Thai origin; report fever, rash, ulcers, bruising.
Lamotrigine: slow titration, report any rash, not for mania; taper anticonvulsants over at least 4 weeks.

summary: You can now apply the MHRA valproate restrictions to men and women under 55 and monitor valproate safely. You know the main hazard and safeguard for carbamazepine and lamotrigine.

A.q: Under current MHRA safety measures, what is needed before valproate is started for the first time in a man aged 30?
options: A negative pregnancy test from his partner first
Written agreement from his GP and the pharmacist
Two specialists agreeing independently in writing
A signed annual risk form from his own consultant
A.why: CG185 box 1: do not start valproate in anyone, male or female, younger than 55 unless 2 specialists independently agree and document that there is no other effective, tolerated treatment or the reproductive risks do not apply.

whyNot.0: A partner's pregnancy test is not the MHRA requirement for starting.
whyNot.1: GP and pharmacist agreement is not the specialist requirement.
whyNot.3: The requirement is two independent specialist opinions, not one consultant's form.

A.q: Which tests are taken when valproate is started for bipolar disorder?
options: Weight or BMI, FBC and liver function tests
Thyroid function, calcium and eGFR levels
ECG, prolactin and creatine kinase levels
A plasma valproate level and a lipid profile
A.why: CG185 1.10.29: measure weight or BMI and carry out a full blood count and liver function tests when starting valproate.

whyNot.2: These are not the baseline valproate tests in NICE CG185.

A.q: A person taking lamotrigine for bipolar depression develops a new rash while the dose is being increased. What should they be advised to do?
options: Apply emollient and mention it at the next review
Contact their doctor immediately
Stay on the current dose until the rash settles
Take an antihistamine and continue increasing
A.why: CG185 1.10.37: advise people to contact their doctor immediately if they develop a rash while the lamotrigine dose is being increased.

whyNot.0: Waiting for a routine review risks a serious skin reaction progressing.
whyNot.2: Holding the dose without medical advice does not get the rash assessed.
whyNot.3: Continuing the titration with a rash is unsafe.

B.q: Wei, 29, of Han Chinese origin, may be started on carbamazepine. Which test should be done before the first dose?
options: Plasma carbamazepine level
Thyroid function tests
Serum lithium level
HLA-B*1502 allele test
B.why: BNF: test for HLA-B*1502 in people of Han Chinese or Thai origin before starting carbamazepine, because the allele is strongly linked to Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

whyNot.0: A drug level cannot be measured before the drug is given.
whyNot.1: Thyroid tests are not the pre-treatment screen for this risk.
whyNot.2: A lithium level is not relevant to carbamazepine.

B.q: Hannah, 31, has taken valproate for bipolar disorder for 2 years. She tells the nurse she would like to try for a baby. What is the best advice?
options: Stop valproate today and tell the team at the next visit
Plan a gradual, supervised stop with her prescriber
Continue valproate and take extra folic acid in pregnancy
Halve the dose herself as soon as she is pregnant
B.why: CG185 1.10.27 and CG192 1.4.28: valproate should be stopped gradually under medical supervision because of fetal malformation and neurodevelopmental risk; she should not stop abruptly.

whyNot.0: Stopping abruptly risks relapse; the change should be planned and supervised.
whyNot.2: Folic acid does not make valproate exposure in pregnancy acceptable.
whyNot.3: Any exposure in pregnancy carries risk, and self-adjusting is unsafe.

B.q: Abdul, 50, takes valproate. His routine LFTs come back clearly abnormal. What does NICE advise?
options: Recheck LFTs in 6 months
Measure a plasma valproate level
Reduce the dose by a quarter
Stop valproate immediately
B.why: CG185 1.10.30: stop valproate immediately if abnormal liver function or a blood dyscrasia is detected.

whyNot.0: Waiting 6 months leaves possible liver injury untreated.
whyNot.1: Levels are not routine and do not address liver toxicity.
whyNot.2: Dose reduction is not the NICE response to abnormal liver function.

C.q: Sofia, 27, has mania and is not taking any antipsychotic or mood stabiliser. The team discusses first treatment. Which option fits NICE CG185?
options: Offer an antipsychotic such as olanzapine
Start lamotrigine with a slow titration
Start valproate as the first-choice drug
Start an SSRI alongside a mood stabiliser
C.why: CG185 1.5.3: if a person develops mania and is not on an antipsychotic or mood stabiliser, offer haloperidol, olanzapine, quetiapine or risperidone.

whyNot.1: CG185 1.5.12: do not offer lamotrigine to treat mania.
whyNot.2: Valproate is not first choice, and MHRA rules restrict starting it under 55.
whyNot.3: Antidepressants should be considered for stopping in mania, not started.

C.q: Luke, 22, takes carbamazepine. He rings the ward helpline with a high temperature, mouth ulcers and new bruising on his legs. What is the most appropriate advice?
options: Take paracetamol and rest for 48 hours
Use an antiseptic mouthwash and continue
Seek immediate medical attention today
Book a routine level at his next clinic
C.why: BNF carbamazepine: people should seek immediate medical attention if fever, rash, mouth ulcers, bruising or bleeding develop, as these may signal a blood disorder.

whyNot.0: Treating the fever at home could miss a serious blood disorder.
whyNot.1: Mouth care does not address possible bone marrow suppression.
whyNot.3: A routine level would delay urgent assessment.

C.q: Ian, 40, is stable on valproate and lamotrigine for bipolar disorder. The team plans to stop lamotrigine. What does NICE recommend?
options: Stop it at once, as valproate covers relapse
Reduce gradually over at least 4 weeks
Reduce over 3 days to limit drug overlap
Stop it once a plasma level has been taken
C.why: CG185 1.10.39: if stopping lamotrigine, reduce the dose gradually over at least 4 weeks to minimise relapse risk.

whyNot.0: Another mood stabiliser does not remove the need to taper.
whyNot.2: Three days is far shorter than the recommended taper.
whyNot.3: Lamotrigine levels are not routine and do not replace tapering.

reteach.title: Match the drug to its danger
reteach.question: What is the key safety rule for each mood stabiliser?

blocks.body: Valproate: under 55, do not start without two independent specialist agreements; prevent pregnancy. Carbamazepine: test HLA-B*1502 where relevant and report fever, rash, ulcers or bruising. Lamotrigine: increase slowly and report any rash. All three: stop gradually over at least 4 weeks.

blocks.text: The under-55 valproate rule applies to men as well as women.

explain.body: Do not start valproate in males or females under 55 unless 2 specialists independently agree and document that no other effective, tolerated treatment exists or reproductive risks do not apply.

test.q: To whom does the MHRA rule on starting valproate in people under 55 apply?
options: Women able to have children
Women and girls of any age
Males and females
People with epilepsy
test.why: CG185 box 1: the under-55 safety measure applies to people, male or female, younger than 55.

whyNot.0: This group has extra measures, but the under-55 rule is wider.
whyNot.1: The rule includes males as well.
whyNot.3: The rule is not limited by diagnosis.

explain.body: Possible association with neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers taking valproate around conception. Advise effective contraception (condoms plus a partner's method) during treatment and for 3 months after stopping.

test.q: For how long after stopping valproate should a man continue effective contraception?
options: 1 month
3 months
6 months
12 months
test.why: CG185 box 1: effective contraception is recommended throughout treatment and for 3 months after stopping valproate.

whyNot.0: One month is shorter than the MHRA advice.
whyNot.2: Six months is longer than the MHRA advice.
whyNot.3: Twelve months relates to advising men planning a family within the next year, not the contraception period.

explain.body: Weight or BMI, FBC and LFTs at the start, after 6 months and then annually. Do not routinely measure plasma levels. Stop immediately if abnormal liver function or blood dyscrasia. Teach people the signs of blood and liver disorders.

test.q: When should plasma valproate levels be measured in bipolar disorder?
options: Every 3 months during the first year
If ineffective, non-adherent or toxic
One week after every single dose change
Every 6 months alongside the LFTs
test.why: CG185 1.10.32: do not routinely measure valproate levels unless there is evidence of ineffectiveness, poor adherence or toxicity.

whyNot.0: Three-monthly levels are a lithium schedule.
whyNot.2: Weekly post-change levels are a lithium rule.
whyNot.3: LFTs are repeated, but levels are not routine.

explain.body: Carbamazepine: HLA-B*1502 testing in people of Han Chinese or Thai origin; report fever, rash, mouth ulcers, bruising or bleeding; hyponatraemia is common. Lamotrigine: slow titration, interaction with valproate, report rash, not for mania.

test.q: Why does lamotrigine need slow dose titration?
options: To prevent early neutropenia
To prevent lithium toxicity
To prevent hyponatraemia
To reduce serious rash risk
test.why: CG185 1.10.36-1.10.37: slow titration and immediate reporting of rash reduce the risk of serious skin reactions with lamotrigine.

whyNot.0: Neutropenia is the classic clozapine risk.
whyNot.1: Lamotrigine titration is not about lithium.
whyNot.2: Hyponatraemia is a common carbamazepine side effect.
